abstract: AVL trees maintain strict height balance through rotations, guaranteeing logarithmic search, insertion, and deletion times. This work presents a detailed, step-by-step exposition of all four rotation cases---single left, single right, left-right, and right-left---implemented in pure Python. We formalize the height-balance invariant, prove its preservation under each rotation, and provide a concise algorithmic description that can be directly mapped to the source code in the public repository. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 49 788.20 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 20 085 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261030_130124_avl_tree_rotations_explained_s}
